data.narrative:
Glyphic Biotechnologies is a Series A biotech company founded by Joshua Yang and Daniel Estandian that has raised $44M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 11 comparable companies: 3 public peers (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private firms including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Chai Discovery.

A stage-progression method is applicable and forms the primary basis for valuation. Using total capital raised ($44M) as a proxy for post-money valuation at the Series Seed/early Series A phase, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—standard for advancement to the next institutional round—yields $88M. This reflects typical Series A to Series B advancement dynamics within biotech.

Peer-median analysis could not be reliably applied due to insufficient clustering of comparables at the same stage and valuation tier; only one adjacent-stage peer met filters. Public comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 5.6x across the three public tickers) cannot be executed without target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. The triangulated range is therefore $75M to $101M, with a median of $88M supported by the stage-progression method alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based valuation inputs, limited narrow-peer data, and stage-to-stage advancement variability specific to biotech risk profiles.
